rows: Ad-hoc BM25 score of a single document against a query (1-doc index; 0.0 if no match)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Compute an ad-hoc BM25 relevance score for one document against a query string, using the English stemmer and a throwaway 1-document index. Returns 0.0 when the document does not match the query. Because BM25 statistics depend on the whole corpus, scores are NOT comparable across rows — use bm25_search to rank a real corpus. NULL document or query → NULL.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Ad-hoc BM25 score of a single document against a query, e.g. `bm25_score('the cat sat on the mat', 'cat')` (> 0.0 on match, 0.0 otherwise).
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Ad-hoc BM25 relevance of a single document against a query.","sql":"SELECT tantivy.main.bm25_score('the cat sat on the mat', 'cat') AS score"}]
rows.vgi.keywords: ["bm25","bm25 score","relevance score","single document","ad-hoc score","full-text match","scoring","ranking probe","query match"]

BM25 full-text ranking of a JSON document corpus against a query, as (doc_id, score) rows

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Rank a corpus of documents against a full-text query by BM25 relevance, using an ephemeral in-RAM tantivy index built per call (English stemmer). The corpus is a constant JSON payload: a JSON array of strings (doc_id = array index) or of {id,text} objects (explicit doc_id); a subquery is not accepted as an argument, so materialize one with SET VARIABLE and pass getvariable(...). Multi-term queries are conjunctive (every term must match); write 'a OR b' to match any term. Returns one (doc_id, score) row per matching document, best score first. NULL/empty corpus or blank query → no rows; malformed JSON or an unparseable query is a clear error.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Rank a JSON document corpus by BM25 relevance to a query, returning `(doc_id, score)` rows best-first, e.g. `bm25_search('["the cat sat","dogs bark"]', 'cat')`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Rank a small JSON corpus by BM25 relevance to a query, best score first.","sql":"SELECT doc_id, score FROM tantivy.main.bm25_search('[\"the cat sat\",\"dogs bark\",\"a cat and a dog\"]', 'cat') ORDER BY score DESC, doc_id"},{"description":"Rank a corpus carrying explicit {id,text} document ids.","sql":"SELECT doc_id, score FROM tantivy.main.bm25_search('[{\"id\":10,\"text\":\"the cat sat\"},{\"id\":20,\"text\":\"stock crash\"}]', 'cat')"},{"description":"Rank product titles for 'running OR shoes' with bm25_search, join the hits back to the titles by id, and use tokenize(…, 'english') to list which stemmed query terms each hit contains.","sql":"SELECT p.title, round(h.score, 3) AS score, list_sort(list_intersect(tantivy.main.tokenize(p.title, 'english'), tantivy.main.tokenize('running shoes', 'english'))) AS matched_terms FROM tantivy.main.bm25_search('[{\"id\":1,\"text\":\"Trail running shoes\"},{\"id\":2,\"text\":\"Leather dress shoes\"},{\"id\":3,\"text\":\"Runners guide to the marathon\"},{\"id\":4,\"text\":\"Cast iron skillet\"},{\"id\":5,\"text\":\"Running socks\"}]', 'running OR shoes') AS h JOIN (VALUES (1, 'Trail running shoes'), (2, 'Leather dress shoes'), (3, 'Runners guide to the marathon'), (4, 'Cast iron skillet'), (5, 'Running socks')) AS p(id, title) ON p.id = h.doc_id ORDER BY h.score DESC, p.title"}]
rows.vgi.title: BM25 Corpus Search & Ranking

Snowball-stem a single word for the given language (e.g. running → run)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Reduce a single word to its Snowball stem (root) for the given language, e.g. 'running' → 'run' in English. Useful for normalizing terms before matching or grouping. NULL word or language → NULL; an unknown language is a clear error.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Snowball-stem one word to its root for a language, e.g. `stem('running', 'english')` → `run`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Snowball-stem a single English word to its root.","sql":"SELECT tantivy.main.stem('running', 'english') AS root"},{"description":"Stem the word 'connections' with every supported Snowball stemmer (one row per language from supported_languages) and keep only the languages whose stemmer changes it.","sql":"SELECT lang, tantivy.main.stem('connections', lang) AS root FROM tantivy.main.supported_languages WHERE tantivy.main.stem('connections', lang) <> 'connections' ORDER BY lang"},{"description":"Tokenize a sentence (no stemming), then stem each token with stem() to group the word variants under their English Snowball root, most frequent root first.","sql":"SELECT tantivy.main.stem(tok, 'english') AS root, list(DISTINCT tok ORDER BY tok) AS variants, count(*) AS occurrences FROM unnest(tantivy.main.tokenize('Runners were running; the runner runs and ran a run.')) AS u(tok) GROUP BY root ORDER BY occurrences DESC, root"}]

Tokenize text into VARCHAR[]; 1-arg form only splits+lowercases (no stemming)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Split text into normalized word tokens, returned as a `VARCHAR` array. Two forms: `tokenize(text)` applies the default analyzer only — unicode word segmentation, lowercasing, and dropping of overly long tokens, with NO stemming (e.g. 'Running quickly, CATS!' → ['running','quickly','cats']); `tokenize(text, lang)` does the same and additionally Snowball-stems each token for the given language, collapsing word variants to a shared root (e.g. 'Running quickly' with 'english' → ['run','quickli']). NULL text (or NULL language in the 2-arg form) → NULL; an unknown language is a clear error.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Tokenize text into a `VARCHAR` array of normalized terms. The 1-arg form `tokenize(text)` only tokenizes and lowercases (no stemmer), e.g. `tokenize('Running quickly, CATS!')` → `['running','quickly','cats']`. The 2-arg form `tokenize(text, lang)` additionally Snowball-stems each token, e.g. `tokenize('Running quickly', 'english')` → `['run','quickli']`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Tokenize text into lowercased word tokens (1-arg form, no stemming).","sql":"SELECT tantivy.main.tokenize('Running quickly, CATS!') AS tokens"},{"description":"Tokenize and Snowball-stem text for a language (2-arg form).","sql":"SELECT tantivy.main.tokenize('Running quickly', 'english') AS tokens"},{"description":"Tokenize a sentence (no stemming), then stem each token with stem() to group the word variants under their English Snowball root, most frequent root first.","sql":"SELECT tantivy.main.stem(tok, 'english') AS root, list(DISTINCT tok ORDER BY tok) AS variants, count(*) AS occurrences FROM unnest(tantivy.main.tokenize('Runners were running; the runner runs and ran a run.')) AS u(tok) GROUP BY root ORDER BY occurrences DESC, root"}]
